Notably, neonates and young infants have immature platelet biology and different CYP2C19 metabolic profiles compared to adults, raising the possibility that the standard weight-based dose (0.2 mg/kg/day) may not have achieved adequate P2Y12 inhibition. The bleeding profile (essentially identical between arms: 87/464 vs 88/436) provides indirect evidence that antiplatelet effect was minimal or absent at this dose in this population, as one would expect at least some differential bleeding signal if meaningful platelet inhibition were occurring. 2. The near-identical bleeding rates between clopidogrel and placebo arms suggest the intended biology (platelet aggregation inhibition) may not have been meaningfully achieved. This is consistent with known pharmacokinetic differences in neonates (reduced CYP2C19 activity, altered drug metabolism). 3. The wide confidence interval spanning zero and the non-significant p-value indicate no meaningful treatment effect. Notably, shunt thrombosis numerically favored placebo (21 vs 26 events), suggesting no benefit on the most mechanistically relevant component. 4. Death: 60 placebo vs 51 clopidogrel (slight numerical favor for clopidogrel but not significant); shunt thrombosis: 21 placebo vs 26 clopidogrel (numerically worse); cardiac procedure: 9 placebo vs 12 clopidogrel (numerically worse). The population itself (neonates and infants) may be a wrong population for standard clopidogrel dosing given immature drug metabolism. 5. CONFOUNDERS: The trial was adequately powered (N=906) and had a clear comparator. The most plausible failure explanation is that the dose used was insufficient to achieve meaningful P2Y12 inhibition in this age group (wrong population/dose for the mechanism), rather than that the mechanism itself is wrong. The lack of any differential bleeding signal strongly suggests inadequate pharmacological effect. This is best classified as a wrong_population failure (neonates/infants with immature CYP2C19 metabolism receiving a dose calibrated without adequate PK/PD data for this age group), with a secondary consideration of no_target_engagement due to likely insufficient drug activation.
